newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Paranagua port operating normally-traders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Paranagua port operating normally-traders.

text.p: The key Brazilian port of Paranagua was operating normally despite a union's claim that portworkers were working on a reduced basis and that loadings were already affected, traders said.
Port officials earlier said the port was operating normally and denied a union official's claim that the port was running at only 50 percent of normal capacity.

"They were talking about a slow-down in operations but it looks like it didn't happen," said a trader at a large export firm. "The latest news I have is that the (vessel) Panli is currently operating at full-speed."
The Panli was programmed to load 55,000 tonnes bulk soybeans, according to Paranagua port records.
"The three quays handling soybeans and soymeal are operating," the trader said.
Another trader confirmed that a scheduled strike at Paranagua on March 5 was not affecting loadings yet.
"It is not affecting operations yet," he said. "The port is operating normally."

Nelson Bandeira, secretary of the Paranagua Unions Council, Said workers planned to strike from 0700 local/1000 GMT on March 5 over demands for a 21 percent increase in wages which they say they did not receive last year.
Other Brazilian ports would then join the strike on March 6 out of sympathy, Bandeira said.
